burst.calibration: same exposure, ISO, WB, black, white and byte-identical per-frame shading maps
burst.operation: Per-frame calibrated linear RGB crop; luminance-pyramid translation; bilinear resampling; valid-overlap robust average with reference residual rejection

calibration.matrixDirection: sensor RGB with separate white balance to linear sRGB, row-major

transformLog: Lossless JPEG predictor-1 unpack, no demosaic or rendering
Use full active array; no crop
Subtract exact rational per-site black levels
Normalize by corresponding white minus black
Bilinear demosaic with clipped neighborhood and renormalized edge weights
Clamp output gamut and sRGB encode
independentDecode: rawpy 0.27.1 / LibRaw 0.22.1: all decoded samples byte-identical. DNG rational black tags retain fractions that rawpy's integer black API rounds down.

reference.relationship: Independent LibRaw rendering of the SAME source DNG for diagnostic comparison; not a Google HDR+ final result, Apple result, or ground truth

adaptations: shading.json is a lossless JSON representation of the supplied TIFF gain map; reference.jpg is a LibRaw-rendered derivative. Browser previews and crops are our own rendered adaptations, CC-BY-SA-4.0.

capabilities.processedImageImport: JPEG/PNG, explicitly synthetic RGGB sampling after browser sRGB conversion

limitations: One validated fixture only; no generic DNG color management
Sidecar lens-shading correction uses an explicit endpoint-aligned bilinear grid approximation
Bilinear demosaic is educational and can produce false color/zippering
Full-frame locator point-samples native reconstructed RGB at stride 6; it is not a quality export
Real fusion is limited to the prepared 384x384 static-region crop, translation only; residual rejection is not semantic motion detection
The original bundled capture has zero saturated sensor sites (maximum 814 vs white 1023); finite-capacity saturation is a labeled schematic
iPhone/Halide capture, actual projector readability, and a spoken ten-minute rehearsal remain unvalidated
